briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The United States launched an unprecedented economic offensive, "Operation Economic Outcast," against Iran, coinciding with escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea and reports of a near-total halt in traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. These developments significantly heighten the risk of direct military confrontation in the Middle East, with both the US and Iran signaling readiness for decisive action.

IRAN
No direct military operations were reported against Iran within its borders. However, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth explicitly stated that military force, including in the Strait of Hormuz, is not ruled out. Economically, Iran is facing severe pressure; the Rial depreciated to over 2,000,000 per USD, and the US sanctioned nearly 60 Iran-linked entities, individuals, and vessels across nuclear, missile, cyber, and oil sectors, with digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping identified for potential secondary sanctions. Shortages of gasoline are reported across major cities like Tehran and Mashhad. Iranian Economy Minister Seyed Ali Madanizadeh claims readiness for sanctions, while President Masoud Pezeshkian warned the US that bullying would not work and called for regional cooperation. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf dismissed US threats as "big talk" that trade partners would ignore. Major General Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, expressed distrust in Washington and called for a change in US behavior. Mohammad Mokhber, a senior advisor to the Leader, warned of a "decisive response" to any continued US miscalculations. Commander-in-Chief of the Army states Iranians are ready to fight for 20 generations to defend their homeland.

ISRAEL
Israeli forces conducted multiple military operations: In Gaza, airstrikes targeted and destroyed two Hamas weapon depots located inside mosques in Shati and Deir al-Balah, claiming dozens of Kalashnikovs and other military equipment. Strikes in Deir al-Balah killed Mohammad Abd al-Nasser Jabr Abu Asaad, a Hamas Nukhba operative involved in the October 7 onslaught, and injured others. Another Hamas Nukhba company commander was targeted in Khan Younis. In the West Bank, the Duvdevan Commando Unit arrested Imam Hazem, son of Fathi Hazem (who was killed last week), in Jenin, for planning a terror attack in Israel; another suspect was arrested in Sanur. Israeli Paratrooper brigades completed three months in Gaza, destroying approximately 13 km of tunnels and terror infrastructure, and are now redeploying to Judea and Samaria. Along the eastern border in the Jordan Valley, IDF forces are sweeping for suspected infiltrators. In southern Lebanon, Israeli forces carried out significant demolition operations in Haris and Mays al-Jabal, and multiple airstrikes in al-Mansouri. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu revealed that Iran attempted to assassinate one of his sons. Israel expressed satisfaction with Trump's economic sanctions on Iran. Netanyahu is scheduled to convene the security cabinet to discuss Gaza, Syria, and Judea and Samaria. Defense Minister Israel Katz and PM Netanyahu issued a "zero tolerance" policy towards terror kites and balloons from Gaza, threatening "powerful actions" and potential evacuations if launches continue, following discoveries of kites in Re'im and Nahal Oz.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces destroyed Hamas weapon depots in mosques and targeted Hamas operatives in Gaza City, Deir al-Balah, Al-Burij, and Khan Younis. One Hamas Nukhba operative, Mohammad Abd al-Nasser Jabr Abu Asaad, was killed in Deir al-Balah. A water desalination plant in Sheikh Radwan, Gaza City, was also hit by an Israeli airstrike. Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem stated that Israel is "destroying all aspects of life in Gaza." Aid trucks to Kerem Shalom will enter at 06:30 due to planned protests by "צו 9" against aid delivery. In the West Bank, Imam Hazem was arrested in Jenin for planning a terror attack, and another Palestinian was arrested in Sanur for similar intentions. The IDF justified its strikes against Hamas operatives by stating they were "systematically violating the ceasefire" by advancing attacks and attempting to restore Hamas capabilities. Terror kites were identified in Re'im and Nahal Oz, prompting strong warnings from Israeli officials.

LEBANON
The Israeli military conducted massive demolition operations on the outskirts of Haris and Mays al-Jabal in southern Lebanon. Israeli fighter jets carried out multiple airstrikes on the town of al-Mansouri and surrounding areas in the Tyre district, southern Lebanon, with one strike identified as being from an Israeli drone in Harris. Lebanese media reported that the US is diplomatically working to resolve the Al-Taher ridge issue, proposing Lebanese army control to ensure the IDF does not reclaim the ridge.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The US State Department officially removed Syria from its list of State Sponsors of Terrorism, after 47 years. Syrian Foreign Minister al-Shibani and other officials reportedly met with Israeli intelligence officials in Jordan. In Iraq, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi is set to declare the full restoration of national sovereignty on September 30, coinciding with the scheduled withdrawal of the US-led coalition. A leader of Hashed al-Sha'abi, Haj Abu Jaafar al-Tamimi, was arrested in Baghdad by Iraqi National Security Service vehicles, leading to subsequent riots by Hashed al-Sha'abi supporters against Prime Minister al-Zaidi, which were dispersed by security forces. Iraqi security forces also reported dismantling a large internet smuggling network and seizing hundreds of thousands of smuggled medicines in Baghdad. An explosion in Palmyra, Syria, killed one person and injured several others. The road to Baghdad International Airport and the Green Zone were temporarily closed due to security concerns, including a visit by the German Army Commander.

GULF STATES
The Saudi national shipping company confirmed its oil tanker "Amzan" was attacked in the Red Sea. Yemeni Houthi forces, via spokesman Yahya Saree, claimed responsibility for striking the "Amzan" tanker off Yanbu with a ballistic missile, causing a fire and damaging its engine room. Saree also claimed additional ballistic missile and drone attacks on Saudi military concentrations in al-Abr, al-Wadea, and al-Kana'is. The UAE installed protective metal structures around its fuel storage tanks amid fears of potential strikes, and satellite imagery indicates an increase in US refueling aircraft stationed in the UAE. French President Emmanuel Macron and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman issued a joint statement emphasizing the need for a diplomatic solution to Iran's nuclear program and calling for the return of normal maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz. TotalEnergies CEO noted increased shipping costs through the Strait of Hormuz, adding approximately $10 per barrel. Oman's Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi is expected to visit Tehran for further negotiations on control of the Strait of Hormuz. UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated that there is "virtually no movement" in the Strait of Hormuz, warning of significant pressure on global food systems.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US Launches "Operation Economic Outcast" against Iran:** Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced an unprecedented economic campaign, sanctioning nearly 60 Iran-linked entities, individuals, and vessels across nuclear, missile, cyber, and oil sectors, and identifying five additional sectors (digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, shipping) for potential secondary sanctions.
2.  **Houthi Ballistic Missile Attack on Saudi Oil Tanker:** Yemeni Houthi forces claimed responsibility for hitting the Saudi oil tanker "Amzan" off Yanbu in the Red Sea with a ballistic missile, causing a fire and damaging the engine room.
3.  **Near Total Halt in Strait of Hormuz Traffic:** UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated that "virtually no movement" is occurring in the Strait of Hormuz, warning of severe implications for global energy, fertilizer, and food supply chains.
4.  **Iranian Rhetoric on US Sanctions and Strait of Hormuz:** Iranian officials, including President Pezeshkian, Parliament Speaker Qalibaf, and IRGC Spokesman Mohebbi, dismissed US sanctions as propaganda and warned of "heavy strategic strikes" on US energy chokepoints if Iran's infrastructure is threatened.
5.  **Israeli Operations in Gaza and West Bank:** IDF destroyed two Hamas weapons depots inside mosques in Gaza (Shati and Deir al-Balah), targeted two Hamas Nukhba operatives (one killed) involved in the October 7 onslaught, and arrested Imam Hazem in Jenin who was planning a terror attack.
6.  **Israeli Airstrikes and Demolitions in Southern Lebanon:** IDF conducted demolition operations in Haris and Mays al-Jabal and multiple airstrikes in al-Mansouri, southern Lebanon.
7.  **US Removes Syria from State Sponsors of Terrorism List:** The US State Department officially removed Syria from its list of State Sponsors of Terrorism, a designation held for 47 years.
8.  **Pakistan Army Chief Visits Tehran Amidst US-Iran Tensions:** General Asim Munir met with Iranian leaders in Tehran, reportedly after a phone call with President Trump, with a focus on regional stability and potential mediation regarding US-Iran negotiations.
9.  **Escalating "Terror Kites" from Gaza:** Several kites were found in Israeli border communities (Re'im, Nahal Oz), prompting Israel to issue a strong ultimatum and threaten escalated military action for continued launches.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are HIGH across multiple fronts. The Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea are active flashpoints, with the Houthi attack on the Saudi tanker and UN reports of minimal traffic signaling a severe disruption to global shipping. The US economic campaign against Iran, coupled with explicit threats of military force, raises the specter of direct confrontation, which Iran has vowed to meet with decisive retaliation against US interests. In Gaza, continued Israeli strikes on Hamas targets, even amidst a ceasefire, and Israel's ultimatum regarding "terror kites," indicate a high likelihood of renewed escalation. Israeli demolitions and airstrikes in southern Lebanon suggest an ongoing low-intensity conflict that could escalate. The arrest of a Hashed al-Sha'abi leader and subsequent riots in Baghdad highlight internal instability that could be exploited by various actors, potentially increasing Iranian proxy influence. Military postures are hardening, with the US not ruling out force, Iran expressing readiness, Houthis asserting a "blockade for blockade" policy, and Israel maintaining offensive operations. Red lines include Iranian nuclear weapons, disruption of oil flow (US), direct military action against Iranian infrastructure (Iran), and attacks on Saudi infrastructure (Saudi Arabia).

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** launched "Operation Economic Outcast" against Iran, sanctioning nearly 60 entities and expanding secondary sanctions to five sectors. Secretary Bessent emphasized a "zero leakage" policy and defined timelines for countries to cease interactions with Iran, threatening loss of access to the US dollar system. Defense Secretary Hegseth explicitly stated military force is not ruled out in the Strait of Hormuz or elsewhere. The US also removed Syria from its list of State Sponsors of Terrorism and canceled a joint amphibious drill with South Korea, citing constraints from the "Iran war." **Saudi Arabia** confirmed the "Amzan" tanker attack and, with **France**, issued a joint statement calling for a diplomatic solution to Iran's nuclear program and freedom of navigation in Hormuz. The **UAE** installed protective metal structures around fuel tanks. **Oman's** Foreign Minister will visit Tehran for Strait of Hormuz talks, suggesting continued mediation efforts. **Russia** saw its President Putin meet the Indian Foreign Minister, and Putin authorized the government to seize critical infrastructure if unprotected against drone attacks. **China**'s President Xi Jinping is expected at the BRICS summit in India, and the US is considering tariffs on Chinese goods and potential sanctions related to Iran. **Pakistan** Army Chief Asim Munir visited Tehran, meeting Iranian leaders, reportedly after a phone call with President Trump, positioning Pakistan as a potential facilitator in the US-Iran crisis. The **UN** Secretary-General Guterres highlighted the near-total halt of traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, warning of global food system pressure.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions exist regarding the status of Strait of Hormuz traffic, with the UN Secretary-General stating "virtually no movement" while a US official claims 7-15 million barrels of oil are still being transported daily. There are conflicting reports and interpretations of Iranian Parliament Speaker Qalibaf's remarks, with Trump quoting him as saying "We are hungry and will not last," which Iranian state media vehemently denies as a fabrication. Netanyahu's claim of an Iranian assassination attempt on one of his sons remains unverified. The nature of the "Board of Peace" mentioned in relation to Israel's ultimatum on Gaza kites lacks specific detail. Initial reports of an Iraqi Counter-Terrorism Service raid on Hashed al-Sha'abi homes were later denied, with Hashed al-Sha'abi officials stating the "confusion has been settled," suggesting internal political sensitivities and potential disinformation. Propaganda indicators are prevalent from all sides, including highly charged language from US officials and Iranian state media, explicit accusations of "fake news," and the symbolic actions of Iranian pro-regime women. Key reporting gaps include the full extent of damage from the Houthi and Israeli strikes, detailed accounts of US-Pakistan-Iran diplomatic discussions, and further clarification on the US cancellation of military drills due to the "Iran war."
